## What

Fixes three causes of flaky tests. Each has a regression test that drives its cause on purpose instead of waiting for a slow host, and fails with the fix removed:

| Flaky test | Cause | Fix | Regression evidence | Base failure evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Browser fixture server port race (`apps/dag-ui-e2e`) | `startFixtureServer` picked a port by opening a probe, closing it and binding the port seconds later. Anything else could take it in between; a restart likewise gave the port up between servers. | The read API binds `127.0.0.1:0` and announces the port it took. `startFixtureServer` keeps holding that port through restarts and relays connections to whichever server is current. `--origin-port` makes the fixture data link to that held port. | `fixture-server.spec.ts`: both journeys squat every port a probe or restart releases, at the moment it is released. Both fail with the base `fixture-server.ts`/`serve-fixture.mjs` and pass with the fix. `dag-ui.spec.ts` holds `serve-fixture.mjs` to refusing `--port 0` without `--origin-port`. | Actions run 41410850207, test-linux job 125163321641: the fixture server exited 2 on `Address already in use`. |
| Windows `live::a_cursor_older_than_the_retained_frames_is_answered_stale` timeout | The poller held the sidebar lock for an entire read of the runs directory, including slow summary-cache writes on Windows, and `GET /api/v2/events` waited on that lock. | `src/live.rs` reads runs without the sidebar lock and takes only the brief lock needed to store what it read. | `tests/e2e/live.rs` `a_stream_and_a_subscription_are_answered_while_the_sidebar_is_reading_a_run` blocks a run's summary read on a FIFO, so the read stalls for as long as the test holds it, and requires streams and subscriptions to answer meanwhile. Fails with the base `src/live.rs`, passes with the fix. | Actions run 41410850207, cross (windows-latest) job 125163458376. |
| Stop-button header journey (`dag-ui-header.spec.ts` "Stop is offered only before a run has ended") | A run written after the poller's last look was missing from a subscription's own snapshot, so the browser took it for unserved and opened a different run. | A subscription reads its run's row when the sidebar lacks it, includes it in the snapshot, and sends it to existing subscriptions. | `tests/e2e/live.rs` `a_run_no_look_has_listed_yet_is_in_the_snapshot_of_a_subscription_to_it` subscribes to a run no look has listed. Fails with the base `src/live.rs`, passes with the fix. | No CI record found among recent failed runs, and the journey passed 10/10 locally against the base server. The evidence is the regression test above failing on the base, plus the earlier local observation that the journey failed about half the time. |

## Not in this change

Two other intermittent journeys are left identical to the base and recorded as follow-ups:

- **Long-body human-item detail** (`dag-ui-human-items.spec.ts`): the attempted fix still depended on Chromium's animated keyboard scroll, which reduced-motion emulation does not turn off. No CI failure of this cause was found, and the journey passed 20/20 locally on the base.

- e2e `live` suite: 25 passed.
- `just fmt-check`, `just lint`, `just lint-llm-validate` and `just lint-llm-diff` pass.

No test is skipped, retried, or given a longer timeout, and no existing assertion is weakened.

## Why

Unrelated CI failures blocked a three-line packaging comment three times and forced a manual merge. Ordinary changes should not stall because another process takes a fixture's port or slow storage stops the live API from answering.

Only advisories against dependency versions newly introduced by a change fail the required audit; existing advisories remain visible without blocking unrelated changes or releases. License, ban, source, yanked-crate and unused-dependency violations still block.

RUSTSEC-2026-0433 against pulldown-cmark blocked every change and forced a manual release merge, even though this crate did not enable the affected feature. ## What

Link onepipeline 0.91.1, which ends a settled run’s observer graph and its command judge processes. Add coverage that the read API never starts, adopts or drives a run, and make the adopted-run shutdown journey independent of host tooling and macOS temporary-path length.

## Why

Stop Codex launches and their helpers consuming network and quota after their work ends ([oneharness#1442](https://github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness/issues/1442)). ai-orchestrator requires its engine and this read API to link the same engine before the host can adopt the fix.

The shutdown journey’s earlier 60-second wait was oneharness’s deliberate redirect-delivery deadline, before shutdown grace begins; the dispatch’s own response reported that the turn “did not end within 60s.” Whether the fixture reached that deadline depended on finding `oneharness` on the host’s PATH. It now explicitly selects an unavailable interrupt client and asserts the resulting delivery failure and grace-driven kill. Its request still allows 91 seconds: the 60-second deadline, one second of grace, and a margin of half the deadline. A separate test checks the mirrored deadline against the linked oneharness source. This fixes the pre-existing race and supersedes its earlier follow-up draft.

The [earlier macOS failure](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/40214960004/job/121233992247) also exposed a control-socket path exceeding macOS’s 104-byte limit; the fixture now uses a short state directory under `/tmp`. body.title: perf: keep the Observatory current from pushed changes instead of refetching
body.body:
## What

Replace browser polling and full-payload refetches with resumable pushed changes for the sidebar and visible Graph, Overall, node timeline or Channel view. Hidden views stop subscribing, and the run header’s activity line updates live. The server uses incremental engine reads and gzip with per-frame flushing.

Add dedicated load telemetry and five budgets covering requests, wire traffic, display lag and server CPU. Ensure quiet graphs fit their canvas on opening, and isolate installation builds so they cannot interfere with concurrently running CLI tests.

## Why

The Observatory stays open for hours on shared hosts. Re-reading whole journals and payloads made even finished-run pages generate hundreds of requests per minute, while live views consumed substantial bandwidth and server CPU. Sending only visible changes keeps those pages quiet and responsive; the budgets guard against regressions.

## Additional info

Schema 25 documents the subscription protocol and adds `run.live_activity`. Healthy subscription streams send patches without repeating snapshots; reconnects replay retained changes, with an explicit reset when resuming is no longer possible. The legacy event stream remains available to existing API consumers. The engine dependency moves to 0.87.1, changing engine types exposed through the crate’s public API; see [engine dependency history](docs/engine-dependency-history.md).

[Committed load telemetry](apps/dag-ui-e2e/telemetry/request-load.json) now comes from a full load run on clean commit `ef9d1d0`, linking engine 0.87.1, and supersedes the earlier measurements at `8821e12`. It records zero observation-window requests per minute on settled, stopped and live run pages, worst single-tab wire traffic of 0.162 MB/min, worst single-tab append-to-display lag p95 of 2.355 seconds, and maximum server CPU of 0.4299 cores per live tab—all within the five budget thresholds. The two-tab variants reach a worst display-lag p95 of 2.182 seconds. Measurements use 150 runs across 30 projects, a 116,000-record live journal, 120-second observation windows, and fresh servers and corpora for each variant. ## Why

The browser’s adopted driver uses this binary’s linked engine, not the host’s CLI. Keeping them aligned lets the host adopt the Linear digest and private-plan homing fixes without browser-adopted runs refusing their own tasks.

Breaking Rust API dependency update: public items carry the engine’s types. The HTTP contract is unchanged; the health report now names engine 0.82.0.
